info.title: Frontera Signal API
info.description: Construction data for the Rio Grande Valley, Texas, paid per call: weekly permits, building-input prices, housing supply and labor for Hidalgo and Cameron counties; commercial projects, projects near an address, company track records with trade licenses, monthly housing permits and filed cost per square foot for Hidalgo, Cameron, Starr and Willacy; Hidalgo County parcel records; shelf prices for common building materials. Every value carries as_of, age_days, cadence and stale (weekly measures go stale after 14 days, monthly measures after 90). dark = the source published nothing that week; no_reading = we have no reading for it. Ranges are {low, high, unit}; approx marks a rounded reading. Not a quote, bid or appraisal. Terms: https://fronterasignal.com/terms/
info.x-guidance:
Frontera Signal sells Rio Grande Valley (South Texas) construction data per call over x402: USDC on Base, no account, no API key.
1. Read the free catalog first: GET https://fronterasignal.com/api/v1 lists every paid endpoint, its price, what it returns, its parameters and a free sample.
2. Free samples: https://fronterasignal.com/data/v1/samples/<endpoint>.json is one real answer per paid endpoint. https://fronterasignal.com/data/v1/index.json carries the latest 4 weeks of each weekly series.
3. Call a paid endpoint without payment: it answers 402 with a JSON body (price, returns, sample, docs, how_to_pay) and a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (base64 JSON, x402 v2). Sign and retry with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header; a 200 carries PAYMENT-RESPONSE with the settlement.
4. Bad or unknown parameters get a free 400 and a valid query with nothing to return gets a free 404, before any payment, as {ok, error, message, docs, allowed}. allowed lists every parameter and its valid values. A payment is never settled on a 4xx or 5xx. nearby and parcel look the address up after the payment is verified, so an address they cannot place is a 404 that is not settled; GET /api/v1/parcel/match checks a parcel address for free first.
Which endpoint: one city or the whole Valley this week -> /api/v1/snapshot. New commercial projects with owner, cost and dates -> /api/v1/projects. Projects within a radius of an address -> /api/v1/nearby. A company track record and its trade licenses -> /api/v1/companies. The Hidalgo County parcel record for an address -> /api/v1/parcel. Filed cost per square foot by county and type of work -> /api/v1/cost-per-sqft. Shelf prices for building materials -> /api/v1/materials. Monthly housing permits by structure type -> /api/v1/series/permits-monthly. Weekly history of permits, input prices, housing supply, labor or forecast grades -> /api/v1/series/<name>. The written weekly issue -> /api/v1/issue.
Every value carries as_of, age_days, cadence and stale. dark and no_reading rows say a week has no reading; nothing is filled with guesses.
MCP clients: https://fronterasignal.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP) serves the catalog, the free samples, the paid URL and price for your parameters and the free series as free, read-only tools.

x-mcp.about: Free and read-only: the paid endpoints and prices, a real sample per endpoint, the exact paid URL for your parameters and the free latest-4-weeks series. Payment stays on the HTTP API.

get.description:
Use to size up the construction market in one Rio Grande Valley city (McAllen, Edinburg, Mission, Pharr, San Juan, Weslaco, Donna, Mercedes, Brownsville, Harlingen) or the whole Valley before you lend, build, buy or sell there: permits, housing units by type, sales-tax trend, months of supply, home values, input and material prices, mortgage rate, labor. Every value is dated. Example: "Is McAllen's housing market oversupplied and are building costs rising this week?"

Returns: One Valley city's (or the whole Valley's) latest permits, monthly housing permits by structure type, sales-tax receipts, housing supply, building-input and material prices, labor conditions, newest commercial projects and this morning's mortgage rate, 10-year yield and diesel price, every value dated.

Free sample (a real answer to /api/v1/snapshot?city=McAllen): https://fronterasignal.com/data/v1/samples/snapshot.json

GET /api answers exactly like this endpoint: same parameters, same price, same answer.

Use to track new housing permits month by month in Rio Grande Valley cities and county areas (Hidalgo, Cameron, Starr, Willacy counties): units and buildings by structure type and valuation since January 2024, with year-to-date totals. Filter by place, county, from and to (YYYY-MM). Covers cities that publish no weekly permits. Example: "How many single-family homes did Brownsville permit each month this year?"

Returns: New housing units and buildings authorized by permit each month, by structure type (single-family, 2 units, 3-4 units, 5 or more) with valuation, for Valley cities and unincorporated county areas, plus each year-to-date total.

Error.description:
One error shape for every refusal. 400 and 404 come before any payment and are free.
unknown_param (400): A query parameter this endpoint does not take. allowed lists the ones it does.
repeated_param (400): The same parameter was sent twice.
missing_param (400): A required parameter is missing.
bad_param (400): A value in the wrong format (date, ISO week, number, length). The message names the parameter.
unknown_value (400): A value outside the list we cover (city, county, item, store, type of work, language). allowed lists the valid ones.
unknown_week (400): No issue was published for that week in that language. allowed.week lists the ones we have.
bad_range (400): from is after to.
no_house_number (400): nearby and parcel need a house number and street; an intersection or a street alone has no single place.
not_covered (400): The place is outside what the endpoint covers. parcel covers Hidalgo County only for now.
no_results (404): The query is valid but nothing matches it. Free.
no_readings (404): Rows exist for that range but every one is dark or no_reading. Free.
no_match (404): No owner or design firm contains that name. Free.
too_few_projects (404): Fewer than 5 usable filings in every group, so there is no statistic to sell. Free; counts are in the body.
not_found (404): No such endpoint or series.
address_not_found (404): nearby and parcel: the address could not be placed on the map or matched to a parcel. Found after the payment is verified; the payment is not settled.
ambiguous (404): nearby and parcel: the address fits several different places or parcels. Add the direction (N, S, E, W). Not settled.
outside_coverage (404): nearby: the address is outside Hidalgo, Cameron, Starr and Willacy counties. Not settled.
not_available (404): parcel: this record is not available from this API. Not settled.
rate_limited (429): parcel/match: too many free lookups from one IP address. Retry after the Retry-After header.
upstream_unavailable (503): nearby and parcel read public records at request time, and that service did not answer in time. Retry in a minute. Not settled.
payment_service_starting (503): The payment service is starting. Retry after the Retry-After header (2 s). Never charged.
payments_not_configured (503): Payments are not switched on for this deployment.

message.description: What was wrong, in a sentence.

param.description: The parameter at fault, when there is one.

allowed.description: Every parameter this endpoint takes, with its type and valid values.

groups.description: too_few_projects only: the count in each county and type of work.

location.description: nearby no_results only: where the address was placed.

coverage.description: nearby no_results only: how many filings have a map point.

price.description: USD per call, paid in USDC.

returns.description: What the paid call answers with, in one line.
